content_preview.title: systemd Merges Optional Rust Support for New Standalone Programs, With Meson Only, No Standard Library and Core Libraries Staying in C for Now
content_preview.summary: systemd merged optional Rust support for new leaf programs on 2026-10-24: Meson not Cargo, no_std, core libraries stay C for now. It is in the 263 development branch; project pages disagree on binary sizes and Meson version.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The systemd project merged support for writing programs in Rust on 2026-10-24, according to the [GitHub record of pull request #44324](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/44324), titled "rust: support programs written in Rust" and authored by Christian Brauner (the merge is stamped 06:21:59 UTC; all GitHub times below are UTC). The support is optional and limited to new standalone programs. [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/os-platforms/2026/10/29/systemd-adds-support-f...

editor_notes.content_quality: News article of 884 words (range 400-1200) with a clear lead, a rules section, a first-program/compiler section, the reasons reported for the design, an explicit section on disagreements between the project's own pages, and an explicit 'What is not known' section. Reported facts are separated from the Herald's own checks, and the Herald's checks are labelled as such (tag check on 2026-11-09, reading of 'on Tuesday' as 2026-11-03, diff-anchor mapping to panic.rs). The title (142 characters, under the 150 limit) keeps all four qualifiers and each is supported: Meson only and no Cargo, no standard library (no_std), optional, and core libraries staying in C with the 'for now' qualifier correctly placed in the body on the sentence the project's CODING_STYLE.md uses it in (existing C code is not ported 'for now').
editor_notes.source_verification: Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article is not about Anthropic or an Anthropic product, names Anthropic nowhere in its headline, summary or lead, and has no Anthropic or 'assisted by Claude' credit passage. Independent-source recount (News, so no Analysis threshold applies): 3 outlets independent of the subject: The Register (Liam Proven, 2026-10-29; adds its own reporting: Brauner's Mastodon posts, the 262-released-about-a-month-ago framing, toolchain version dates and context), Phoronix (Michael Larabel, 2026-11-04; reports the Brauner/Poettering blog post with a verbatim closing quote, mostly restating it), Linuxiac (two articles, 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-07, counted as ONE outlet; the first restates the PR description including its 32 KB/20 KB figures, the second restates the blog post). Primary sources (the project's own records, not independent): GitHub systemd PR #44324, PR #44114, the tags page and five files pinned to merge commit 021112961bd64aec54a1f1e6a6c8fda8b732b705, plus rust-lang/rust PR #164855 (the Rust project's own record, independent of systemd). Allowlist: github.com, theregister.com, linuxiac.com and phoronix.com are all in config/source_allowlist.txt (no additions needed). Snapshots: all 14 fetched with HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for every source (no scanner findings, nothing to override). The 10 GitHub snapshots are JavaScript-heavy HTML pages, so I read the raw data instead through the GitHub API and raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit (route recorded; sha256 of raw files: NEWS 571af060988ba22b..., docs/CODING_STYLE.md 10e7765c95d456ad..., docs/HACKING.md 3ee1f03880512e85..., README fe4cd972ffc4b329..., meson.build 31d7d4c0de358f73..., src/rust/systemd-shared/panic.rs 7e02692fce34bc64... (first 16 hex digits)), plus the stored snapshots source-0/1/2/9. The Register (source-10), Linuxiac (source-11, source-12) snapshots were read as extracted text. Phoronix (source-13): the live page returns a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge (HTTP 403 with a browser User-Agent); the stored snapshot is the Archive.org capture web.archive.org/web/20261106052819/https://www.phoronix.com/news/systemd-Loves-Rust, and I re-fetched that capture independently: sha256 fb82c76bb1b437af34897bb48c679e5a8faec0ceb8c4fb7d9af0463bcdf454b6, identical to the manifest hash. Claim-by-claim results. PR #44324 (API): authored by brauner, created 2026-10-20T15:05:12Z, merged 2026-10-24T06:21:59Z into main, merge commit 021112961bd6 (so the 06:21:59 UTC stamp and the 2026-10-24 date are right; the basis is UTC, which the article states). NEWS at that commit: 'CHANGES WITH 263 in spe:' lists 'systemd may now optionally be built with support for programs written in Rust ... rustc >= 1.85, bindgen >= 0.71.1 and meson >= 1.4.0'. Tags: the GitHub API lists 477 tags and none starts with 263 (latest are v262.2, v262.1, v262, v262-rc*); the Herald's own check is labelled as such and was reproduced by me on 2026-11-09. docs/CODING_STYLE.md '## Rust': 'Rust is only used for new leaf components, i.e. programs that nothing else in the tree depends on. Existing C code is not ported to Rust for now, and libsystemd-shared, libsystemd, the NSS and PAM modules and everything else other components depend on stay C.' (the article's quote is verbatim; 'for now' is attributed to the sentence about porting existing C code, which is where the document puts it); 'Rust code is built with meson only. cargo is not used.' (verbatim); 'Only the core and libc crates are permitted. std, alloc and any other crate are not, hence all Rust code is #![no_std].' (supported); 'Rust code only interfaces with the rest of systemd through C linkage' (supported). docs/HACKING.md: 'Rust support is optional. It requires rustc 1.85, bindgen 0.71.1 ... and meson 1.4.0 or newer. With the default -Drust=auto, Rust support is turned off if the toolchain is missing or too old, while -Drust=enabled makes the build fail instead' (supported). The Register (2026-10-29): 'released systemd version 262 about a month ago. That means that systemd 263 is now under construction' (supported); 'this does not indicate the start of an effort to rewrite systemd in Rust. All it means is that new systemd modules can be written in Rust.' (verbatim). PR #44114 (API): 'keyring-setup: add systemd-keyring-setup', merged 2026-10-27T09:27:22Z, body 'It's the first program in systemd written in Rust' and 'enrolls X.509 certificates from the VOA hierarchy into the kernel's .dm-verity, .fs-verity and .bpf keyrings at boot' (supported; the article's quote 'the first program in systemd written in Rust' is a verbatim fragment). Linuxiac 2026-10-24: 'Its implementation is being developed separately' (the article's 'had said' is accurate and dated; the program merged three days later, which the article states without implying Linuxiac was wrong); 'Builds that enable all available features will need the appropriate Rust compiler and bindgen dependencies or must disable Rust support' (supported). rust-lang/rust PR #164855 (API): 'Stop mangling rust_eh_personality again for now', author bjorn3, created 2026-10-24T13:59:49Z, merged 2026-10-24T20:21:21Z (so 'opened on 2026-10-24' and 'merged at 20:21:21 UTC the same day' are right); the description says 'Some projects manually define rust_eh_personality as they use no_std ...'; bjorn3's comment (14:00:30Z): 'The motivation for this PR is https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/44324/files#diff-e904184b81a2...R65'; Mark-Simulacrum asked 'Is the assumption here that this is a "temporary" revert ...?' and bjorn3 answered 'Yeah, this would be temporary until a better solution is found.' (verbatim). The anchor hash e904184b81a2... equals sha256('src/rust/systemd-shared/panic.rs') (computed by me) and line 65 of that file at the merge commit is 'extern "C" fn rust_eh_personality() -> ! {', which confirms the article's labelled Herald mapping. The article does not claim the Rust PR was caused by anything beyond the author's own stated motivation. Phoronix (4 November 2026, 07:44 AM EST): 'Systemd lead developers Christian Brauner and Lennart Poettering who recently started the Amutable company ... wrote a blog post on Tuesday' and the closing quote 'systemd would also like to see Rust adopted in core components and is willing to engage with the Rust community to make this a reality.' (verbatim fragment of the quoted paragraph). Calendar check: 2026-11-03 is a Tuesday and 2026-11-04 a Wednesday, so the article's reading of 'on Tuesday' as 2026-11-03 is right and is labelled as the Herald's reading; the uncited Amutable blog index also dates the post '3 Nov 2026' (used only as a cross-check; no fact from it reached the article). The reasons list is attributed to Linuxiac's 2026-11-07 summary of the two developers' post and each item is in that text: central libraries including libsystemd-shared.so stay C because of Rust's lack of first-class shared library support and a stable ABI (duplicated Rust code, 'more than 180 binaries'); Cargo rejected in favour of Meson alone to avoid two build systems, with security and supply-chain concerns cited; third-party crates not ruled out but wanted more experience first; no rewriting of established components merely to change language, citing filesystem path handling rather than memory safety; Rust support to stay optional because Rust does not support every architecture systemd supports. The reasons are attributed to the two people as reported, not offered as the Herald's analysis. Disagreements (both reported with attribution, neither reconciled, which policy item 6 requires): (1) binary size: PR #44324 description 'Per HACKING.md the stripped test-cli-rust binary is 32 KB with LTO against 20 KB for its C twin' versus merged HACKING.md '`test-cli-rust` is 29 KB, 24 KB with `-Db_lto=true`, `test-cli-c` is 16 KB' (both verified at the pinned commit; no cited source explains the difference; the git history shows the 29/24/16 figures were in the docs commit 66412c31b of 2026-10-23, so the description's wording 'Per HACKING.md' evidently refers to an earlier draft, which is the Herald-independent inference I make here and which the article does not need to state); (2) minimum Meson: README at the commit 'meson >= 0.62.0 / >= 1.8.0 is required to build programs written in Rust' versus PR description 'meson >= 1.4.0', NEWS 'meson >= 1.4.0', HACKING.md 'meson 1.4.0 or newer' and meson.build (line 386 'if meson.version().version_compare('< 1.4.0')' for the Rust check; the project-wide floor in the same file stays '>= 0.62.0', which the article's phrase 'build file check' handles). Repo text at HEAD today (main at 013e8e46625d, 1208 commits after the merge commit): the README still says '>= 1.8.0 is required to build programs written in Rust', HACKING.md still says 29 KB/24 KB/16 KB and meson 1.4.0, so the disagreements persisted and the article's claims are about the pinned merge commit, which it states. Absence and quantifier tests (grep run on title, summary and body): 'None of the cited sources gives a release date for systemd 263' holds against all 14 sources (NEWS says only '263 in spe' and 'the next release (v263)'; The Register says 'under construction'; the PR pages show 'No milestone'); 'none of the cited sources says whether [the Arch and openSUSE OBS failure] has since been resolved' holds (PR #44324 description is the only place that mentions it; the PR conversation and the other thirteen sources are silent); 'only' / 'all' in 'Only the core and libc crates ... so all Rust code is #![no_std]' hold per CODING_STYLE.md; 'Rust code talks to the rest of systemd only through C linkage' holds per CODING_STYLE.md; 'libsystemd-shared, libsystemd, the NSS and PAM modules and everything else other components depend on stay C' is a verbatim list; 'both' (Brauner and Poettering both described as lead developers who started Amutable) holds per Phoronix. No relative dates remain (the Register's 'about a month ago' is a quoted report, followed by calendar dates); dated reports run in chronological order. Internal link /article/2026-09/26-systemd-262-ships-a-statically-linked-container-binary-linux-617-coredump-sockets-and-openssl-4-support exists (published 2026-09-26, no corrections record) and is described only as the Herald's earlier report on the 262 release, which is accurate. Originality: no earlier Herald article covers systemd's Rust support (the closest are the 262 release article and the AGENTS.md canary article); no open PR duplicates it. Not extended: the article makes no Rust-for-Linux kernel comparison and no claim beyond the sources. Scanner and injection: no suspicious_patterns on any source; no instruction-like text found in the pages used.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every claim, quote, number, date and version traced to raw source text; no hallucinated quotes, no misattribution, no orphan URLs (the 14 body links match article.sources; the internal /article/ link is not a source). The 'for now' qualifier is attributed to the right sentence (not extended to the shared-library statement), the Phoronix 'on Tuesday' reading is labelled as an inference and is correct, the reasons are attributed to the two developers as reported by Linuxiac, and the two source disagreements are reported with attribution and unreconciled. The one nuance a careful reader might want is that Linuxiac's 2026-10-24 report words the 20 KB figure as 'its C equivalent built with link-time optimization' whereas the PR description puts the LTO qualifier on the Rust figure; the article quotes the PR description verbatim and says only that Linuxiac 'repeated' the figures, which is accurate, so no correction is warranted.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no editorializing, no superlatives, no AI self-reference. Uncertainty is stated in its own section.
editor_notes.originality: New topic; the only earlier systemd coverage is the 262 release article (linked) and the AGENTS.md AI-canary article. Adds the primary-source reading of the merged rules and the unreconciled documentation disagreements that the secondary outlets do not report.
concerns: Minor and not a correction: the title's 'Core Libraries Staying in C for Now' compresses two statements (CODING_STYLE.md: existing C code is 'not ported ... for now' and the shared libraries 'stay C'; Phoronix: Rust cannot be used in core components 'until there is first-class shared library support'). Both support the headline qualifier and the body attributes each correctly.

The Register's article says the earlier effort #44144 was split into five parts while the PR #44324 description says a stack of four (later five in #44114's description); the article uses neither number, so nothing to correct.
recommendations: Future follow-up if systemd 263 is tagged: report whether the README 1.8.0 and HACKING.md size figures were reconciled and whether the Arch and openSUSE OBS packaging issue was resolved.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced News article; every claim in the headline, summary and lead is backed by the merged repository text, the GitHub API records and three independent outlets, and no correction is required. APPROVE. Featured candidacy: 2 - systemd adopting Rust (optional, leaf programs only) is a notable language and build-policy shift for a foundational piece of most Linux distributions, of interest beyond one project's users, though the first program is small and core libraries stay C.
